Developing grnland

Source: DEVELOPMENT.md

This document describes how the package works and how to extend it. For a user-level introduction, see the README and vignette("grnland").

Setup

You need R, a C++ compiler, and the packages in DESCRIPTION (Rcpp, RcppArmadillo, plus ambient, ggplot2, knitr, rmarkdown and testthat for the suggested features). For development, also install devtools, roxygen2 and pkgdown.

git clone git@github.com:diogro/grnland.git
cd grnland
R CMD INSTALL .
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'

Architecture

A simulation chains four pieces, each replaceable on its own:

model  ──►  develop(model, genotypes, x_start)  ──►  phenotypes  ──►  landscape(X)  ──►  fitness
  ▲                                                                                       │
  └──────────── simulate_population(): selection, reproduction, mutation ◄────────────────┘

Models (R/model.R, R/linear.R)

A model is a list with a class, and these fields: genes, n_genes, traits (indices of the selected genes), loci (a data frame with one row per evolvable parameter: name, code/param, i, j) and x0 (the default starting expression state).

Class Constructor Development
hill_grn grn(), paper_motif() C++ (src/hill.cpp)
custom_grn grn_custom() R port of the same solver (custom_develop_one())
linear_gp gp_linear() closed form, X = G B'

grn() parses edges into a regulation matrix (parse_regulation()), expands evolvable into loci (hill_loci()), and resolves traits.

Development (R/develop.R, src/hill.cpp)

develop() is an S3 generic returning list(X, status): the full expression state of every individual and a status code (0 ok, 1 no convergence, 2 unstable, 3 non-finite).

For Hill networks, hill_develop_cpp() takes the base parameters, the locus table, a genotype matrix and starting states, and for each individual:

  1. writes the genotype into the network parameters (apply_genotype());
  2. integrates the ODE with adaptive Dormand–Prince 5(4) until the right-hand side is small (1e-5);
  3. polishes the steady state with Newton’s method to tol. It accepts the result only if it is non-negative and stays near the integrated state, so it cannot jump to another branch. Otherwise it integrates further, to tol;
  4. checks stability from the eigenvalues of the Jacobian.

Starting states matter for multistable networks (e.g. motif 5): during simulations every offspring starts development from its parent’s state, so populations stay on their branch unless mutation pushes them off it.

Derivatives

hill_derivs_cpp() returns the right-hand side f, the Jacobian J and df/dp for every locus, all analytical. From these,

  • sensitivity(): S = dx*/dp = -J^{-1} df/dp (implicit function theorem);
  • m_matrix(): M = S_T Σ S_T', where S_T holds the rows of the trait genes and Σ = ploidy · μ · diag(σ²);
  • genotype_at(): inverts the map. When the loci are exactly the alphas, the steady-state equations are linear in alpha and are solved directly; otherwise it runs Newton’s method on the loci using S.

Custom models use the user’s Jacobian if given, otherwise finite differences.

Landscapes (R/landscape.R)

A landscape is a function from an n × d phenotype matrix to n fitness values, with class grn_landscape and attributes n_dim and info. The attribute is n_dim and not dim, because structure() refuses to set dim on a function. landscape_grid() precomputes a 2D landscape and interpolates bilinearly. With Perlin noise this matters: ambient has a large fixed cost per call, so caching makes simulations about three times faster.

find_peaks() scans a grid in 2D, merging maxima closer than merge cells. That stops flat tops from producing duplicate peaks. In other dimensions it runs multistart optim().

Perlin noise from ambient is exactly flat along x within some lattice cells, on the lines y · frequency = k + ½. Expect degenerate critical points there. lande_separatrices() ignores them and points at the domain edge.

Simulation (R/simulate.R)

State: alleles A (N × L × ploidy; for diploids each copy carries half the starting value), expression X (N × n_genes), fitness W, and a flag for individuals whose development failed. Each generation:

  1. Selection. selection(W) turns fitness into sampling weights. The default selection_relative_min() is the original scripts’ w - min(w) + 0.001.
  2. Reproduction. Clonal reproduction resamples individuals. Sexual reproduction samples mothers and fathers (from separate halves when sexes = TRUE) and builds gametes with free recombination.
  3. Mutation. Draws the number of mutations from Binomial(N·L·ploidy, μ), adds Normal(0, σ) effects, and clamps the alleles to [lower, upper].
  4. Development. Only individuals whose genotype changed are developed again, starting from their parent’s expression state. Failed developments are lethal (fitness NA, weight 0) or, with invalid = "reject", the mutation is undone.
  5. Recording and stopping. Every record_every generations it stores means, the phenotypic covariance and optionally M at the mean genotype. Every stop$every generations the stopping rule is checked.

The cost is dominated by development of changed individuals and by landscape evaluation. At the paper’s settings a generation takes about 1 ms with a cached landscape.

Lande separatrices (R/lande.R)

For deterministic evolution dz/dt = G ∇W, with G ∝ M(z) (or a fixed G), it works as follows: 1. Evaluate the landscape on a grid and take finite-difference gradients and Hessians. 2. Find critical points by Newton’s method from a lattice of seeds, and keep the non-degenerate saddles. 3. Trace the stable manifold of each saddle backwards with RK4.

Because G is positive definite, the critical points and their types are the same as those of the landscape.

Extending

A new locus type for Hill networks (e.g. a basal-expression term): 1. Add the parameter to the dynamics in rhs() and jac() in hill.cpp. 2. Give it a new code in apply_genotype() and its derivative in dfdp(). 3. Handle the new class name in hill_loci(). 4. Add a finite-difference test of sensitivity().

A new model class: 1. Write a constructor returning the fields listed under Models. 2. Write a develop.<class>() method. 3. If sensitivity(), genotype_at() and default_genotype() can’t use the generic code, add branches for the class. Everything downstream, including m_matrix() and simulate_population(), then works unchanged.

A new landscape: wrap any function with landscape_function(f, dim), or write a constructor that calls new_landscape().

A new selection scheme or stopping rule: a selection scheme is a function from fitness to weights. A stopping rule is a list with every and fun(X) -> peak index or NULL. See stop_at_peaks().

Testing

  • test-motifs.R: the general solver against the closed forms of the paper’s motifs (steady states to about 1e-8, and the sensitivities of Fig2.r).
  • test-general.R: edge parsing, loci, finite-difference derivative checks, custom vs Hill models, linear maps, lande_separatrices().
  • test-simulate.R: hill-climbing, reproducibility from a seed, diploid sexual runs, find_peaks(), landscape_grid() accuracy.

Keep tests fast (the whole suite runs in about a minute) and seeded.

Documentation

  • Roxygen comments in R/ generate man/ and NAMESPACE: run devtools::document().
  • vignettes/grnland.Rmd is a real vignette, built by R CMD check; it must run in seconds.
  • vignettes/articles/paper-figures.Rmd is pkgdown-only (excluded in .Rbuildignore). It shows code without running it and embeds images from vignettes/articles/figures/, which are copied from analysis/figures/. When the full figure runs are done, copy the new images over.
  • The site: pkgdown::build_site() writes docs/, which is committed and served by GitHub Pages from main/docs. Equations use MathJax (math-rendering: mathjax in _pkgdown.yml).

Paper analyses

analysis/ reproduces the paper figures; analysis/README.md lists scripts, settings and run times. Scripts share common.R, cache results in analysis/output/ and accept QUICK=1, N_CORES, REDO=1. Always cap BLAS threads (OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 etc.) when running them in parallel.

Releasing

  1. Bump Version in DESCRIPTION.
  2. Run devtools::document(), devtools::test(), then R CMD build . && R CMD check --no-manual grnland_*.tar.gz.
  3. Rebuild the site with pkgdown::build_site() and commit docs/.
  4. Tag the release (git tag v0.x.y) and push the tag.
